flawed_step: Step 6: independence of N(v) does not justify recoloring every neighbor of v with one color, because such a recoloring can create monochromatic edges from N(v) to vertices outside N(v).
counterexample: The 11-vertex Mycielski graph of C5: vertices v_i,u_i (i modulo 5) and w; edges v_iv_{i+1}, u_iv_{i-1}, u_iv_{i+1}, and wu_i. It is triangle-free but not 3-colorable.
assessment_summary:
Attempted proof and audit:

1. Use induction on the number n of vertices. — JUSTIFIED: induction is an applicable proof method for finite graphs.

2. Every triangle-free graph with n≤3 is 3-colorable. — JUSTIFIED: assigning distinct colors to its vertices gives a proper coloring.

3. Assume every triangle-free graph with fewer than n vertices is 3-colorable, and let G be a triangle-free n-vertex graph. — JUSTIFIED: this is the induction hypothesis and setup.

4. Choose v∈V(G); then G−v is triangle-free and hence has a proper 3-coloring. — JUSTIFIED: deleting a vertex cannot create a triangle, so the induction hypothesis applies.

5. The neighborhood N(v) is an independent set. — JUSTIFIED: an edge between two neighbors of v would form a triangle with v.

6. Recolor all vertices of N(v) with one common color while preserving a proper coloring of G−v. — NOT JUSTIFIED: although vertices in N(v) are mutually nonadjacent, a recolored neighbor may be adjacent to a vertex outside N(v) having the chosen color.

7. Give v either of the two remaining colors. — NOT JUSTIFIED in the actual argument: this would work only after the unsupported recoloring in Step 6 had produced a proper coloring.

8. Therefore G is 3-colorable, completing the induction. — NOT JUSTIFIED: the induction step depends on Steps 6–7 and has not been established.

Verification that the statement is false:

9. Define H with vertices v_i,u_i for i modulo 5 and one vertex w, with edges v_iv_{i+1}, u_iv_{i-1}, u_iv_{i+1}, and wu_i. — JUSTIFIED: this defines a finite simple graph.

10. H contains no triangle involving w. — JUSTIFIED: every neighbor of w is a vertex u_i, and no two u-vertices are adjacent.

11. H contains no triangle avoiding w. — JUSTIFIED: the v-vertices induce the triangle-free cycle C5; the u-vertices are independent; and the two v-neighbors v_{i-1},v_{i+1} of any u_i are nonadjacent in C5. Thus H is triangle-free.

12. Suppose, for contradiction, that H has a proper coloring with three colors. — JUSTIFIED: this is a valid contradiction assumption.

13. Rename the color of w as color 3. Every u_i then has color 1 or 2. — JUSTIFIED: each u_i is adjacent to w.

14. On the v-cycle, replace the color of each v_i having color 3 by the color of u_i, leaving all other v-colors unchanged. This gives a proper coloring of C5 using only colors 1 and 2. — JUSTIFIED: adjacent v-vertices cannot both originally have color 3. If only v_i on an edge v_iv_j is recolored, then u_i is adjacent to v_j by construction, so its color differs from that of v_j; edges whose endpoints are unchanged remain proper.

15. C5 has no proper coloring with two colors. — JUSTIFIED: colors must alternate along a cycle in any 2-coloring, which is impossible when the cycle length is odd.

16. Hence H is triangle-free but not 3-colorable, so the stated universal claim is false. — JUSTIFIED: Steps 11 and 15 contradict the assumed 3-coloring and provide a counterexample.
